text: Quality Assurance Inspector

My name is David Fischbein and I am running for Fullerton City Council to bring proven leadership, accountability, and practical problem-solving to District 5. As a retired U.S. Navy veteran, I spent years leading people, managing resources, solving problems under pressure, and completing missions where preparation and accountability mattered.

My military service included leadership in aviation and maritime operations, including overseas deployments supporting U.S. missions. I was responsible for personnel, equipment, safety, maintenance, and operational readiness. In one aviation assignment, I supervised a 25-sailor work center supporting 12 helicopters and helped reduce aircraft downtime by 25%.

My civilian career has built on those skills through purchasing, supply chain management, quality assurance and government acquisition. I've managed relationships with dozens of vendors, supported millions of dollars in annual sales, and handled government purchases ranging from $10,000 to $250,000. I also hold a B.S. in Business Administration.

Fullerton deserves a councilmember who will focus on responsible spending, safer streets, well-maintained infrastructure, responsive city services, and transparent government. I'll bring a mission-focused approach to District 5: listen to residents, understand the facts, manage resources responsibly, and deliver measurable results. I'll work with residents, staff, businesses, and councilmembers to deliver results.

text: Chemist

Growing up in a working-class family during the 2008 financial collapse, I saw firsthand how quickly a family can go from comfortable to crisis. After working two jobs while earning my degree in Chemistry from UC Davis, I joined the Fullerton community knowing the importance of hard work and cooperation. I ask for your vote as a neighbor with experience making the city work for all of us.

Over the past few years, I’ve volunteered helping families access food and school supplies and served on the Parks and Recreation Commission. That experience has taught me that good governance involves listening to residents, solving problems, and delivering results.
Once elected, I promise to:
Protect public safety funding to ensure strong response times.
Expand funding for our Senior Mobility Program and increase access to community centers and services.
Invest in small business development and social spaces throughout downtown to streamline permitting and increase foot traffic for businesses along Harbor.
I’m honored to be endorsed by:

Councilmember Ahmad Zahra
Councilmember Shana Charles
Fullerton School Board Trustee Vanesa Estrella

text: Fullerton Commissioner/Businessowner

The son of immigrants, I was born and raised in Fullerton. My parents taught me the value of education: I graduated from Fullerton schools, and I earned my Civil Engineering degree at Stanford University.
My wife is a public school counselor, and we decided to raise our two children here in my hometown of Fullerton, where I’ve grown our family’s construction business.

I love Fullerton. My service to our city includes:
Chair, Fullerton Planning Commission
Fullerton Parks and Recreation Commissioner
Fullerton Transportation and Circulation Commissioner
Team Leader, Love Fullerton
Fullerton Sunrise Rotary
That volunteer work includes:
Monthly Truslow Park cleanup
Native garden at Ford Park
Adopting Union Pacific Park
Mobile food pantry at Fullerton churches and parks
Upcoming mobile dental clinic

If you elect me to represent our community on Fullerton’s City
Council, I will:
Ensure Fullerton police and firefighters have the resources they need to protect our safety
Improve Fullerton roads
Enhance Fullerton parks and public spaces
Balance and audit Fullerton’s budget with more transparency
Build senior citizen and workforce housing in Fullerton
Protect the character of our neighborhoods and our quality of life
I will always be accessible to you: call me anytime at (714) 519-6129, email valadez4fullerton@gmail.com, or visit www.valadezforfullerton.com.
I respectfully ask for your vote.
